title: Deciding to be a musician and his father's objection to guitar players
summary: His father refused him a guitar because guitarists were pimps and rounders with gold teeth; Randolph says he might have become a guitarist like Joe Pass.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, did the teachers frown on your listening to James P. Johnson and other rolls?

Well, no, they didn't. No, they didn't because I heard a teacher mention about some player -- somebody playing the piano and she said he was sit his fingers down and all his fingers would be playing the chords. But I had little pieces and things that I would play that had the girls around fanning me, you know, the girls would fan me while I'd be playing the pieces and, oh, my goodness. I thought was just in heaven, just rising, having those girls be fanning me and playing.
Is that the time that you decided that you were going to be a musician?

I decided that I was going to be a musician way back when I was fooling around with the guitar before I ever went to school. I was going to play because that fascinated me. That music was -- and I told my father to get me a guitar andhe said, "Huh-uh, no guitar." You know, he had a hang-up on that [point], that's a terminology musicians use a lot of times. It's because he said guitar players was pimps and rounders. Well, he was right in a way about some of those guitar players, because I remember how they were dressed. They had a Stetson hat and a blue serge trousers,
a starched and ironed jumper, starched -- white starched shirt and the collar standing open, and they'd have all of this gold --

-- on their teeth, and they would have the guitar strung around and they'd have a gang of women behind them just like that. And they were playing and grinning but they're not tickled, you know why they're grinning --
Like Jelly Roll Morton with his diamond in his front tooth.
And that was the bag he didn't want me to get into.
I wouldn't have gotten into that bag. All I wanted -- if I -- I wished now, the way, if you've heard some of Joe Pass --
If you've heard some of Joe Pass, that --
I've known Joe for many years.
